site.title: A design system built for AI to generate against.
site.lede: Humans own the taste: tokens, components, the rules. An agent assembles screens from them. Evals decide what ships. The meal planner above is the test subject, built partly by hand and partly by the agent, and it has to pass the same gate either way.
site.loop.title: The loop
site.loop.desc: Intent goes into a constrained system, the agent generates against it, the eval gate passes or fails it, and every failure either becomes a fix or a change to the system.

site.stack.title: The stack, and why
site.stack.lede: A static React app built with Vite, hosted free on GitHub Pages. There's no server because nothing needs one: your recipes and plans stay in your browser. The test was simple: the smallest setup where every rule can be checked automatically.
site.stack.vite: Instant dev server and sub-second builds, so the agent's edit, check, fix loop stays fast. Vitest shares its config, and ?raw imports bring markdown and test fixtures in as plain text.
site.stack.react: Components with typed props are themselves a guardrail: an agent can't pass a prop the system doesn't have, and TypeScript says so before the browser does.
site.stack.css: Plain CSS scoped per component, every value from generated tokens. Easy for Stylelint to police, and no styling library for an agent to misuse.
site.stack.hosting: Hash routes (#/app) work on any static host with no server config, and GitHub Pages deploys straight from the repo.
site.stack.gate: ESLint, Stylelint, Vitest, Playwright and axe-core run as one command, npm run eval, on demand.
site.stack.next: Server rendering and API routes this app doesn't need, plus more framework conventions for an agent to get wrong.
site.stack.astro: Excellent for content sites, but this is an interactive app, screen after screen.
site.stack.cra: Deprecated, with slower builds and an older toolchain.
site.stack.library: A faster start, but the point is our own system. An agent would reach for components we don't own or control.
